note: Curated routes. A "tube" route carries a full local frame and drives the travelling constriction of the peristalsis profile; a "glow" route carries one number per vertex — how far along the structure that vertex is — and drives a travelling light only, moving nothing. Each route names the anatomical structures at its two ends INSTEAD of coordinates, so the ordering is justified by the atlas's own neighbouring meshes and the taught sequence rather than by a hand-typed point, and the generator refuses an anchor the model does not actually place against the mesh. 'far' means the topologically opposite end of the same mesh, used where the neighbouring structure is not in the model at all or where its nearest vertex is measurably not at an end. 'from' is always the UPSTREAM end and 'to' the downstream one, so the derived parameter is 0 where the source says the flow starts; a glow route also names the CIRCUIT it belongs to and, where it continues another route, the route it comes after, so one crest crosses a chain of separate meshes as a single wave instead of restarting on each. sourceRefs carry the direction-and-mechanism claim; wave rate, width, depth and crest sharpness are display parameters and are NOT claimed from any source.
